thread:
maria: FYI I'm seeing a reproducible burst of immediate retries from the Android SDK after a socket reconnect on the emulator. Looks like okhttp's backoff state is getting reset when the connection closes and then reconnects, so we lose jitter and hit backend hard. Repro steps below.

maria: Steps: 1) Start sampleapp on Android 11 emulator; 2) Send a streaming request that keeps a persistent connection; 3) Kill ADB network (adb emu network down) for ~2s, bring it back; 4) observe 3 quick retries within 100ms each in logs.

maria: Logs snippet: ```
I/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate
I/OkHttp: <-- HTTP FAILED: java.net.SocketException: socket closed (attempt=1)
I/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate (retry)
I/OkHttp: <-- HTTP FAILED: java.net.SocketException: socket closed (attempt=2)
I/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate (retry)
```

alex: Hmm. Are you using the SDK's built-in retry interceptor or relying on OkHttp default RetryAndFollowUpInterceptor?

maria: Using the SDK wrapper which delegates to Retrofit -> OkHttp. We didn't override RetryAndFollowUpInterceptor. Config: OkHttp 4.10.0, Retrofit 2.9.0, target sdk 31.

jordan: Could be related to connect vs stream failures. If the connection is closed mid-stream, okhttp might treat it differently and not apply the exponential backoff state we expect. Do you see connect attempts with different backoff timestamps?

maria: I grep'd timestamps, they are basically consecutive within ms. No exponential spacing. Also noticed no randomized jitter applied.

sasha: Does the server return any Retry-After header or 503 that's confusing the client?

maria: No server-side 503s. Pure client-side socket closed errors.

alex: Two quick things to try: 1) bump to OkHttp 4.11.x (there were some connect retry fixes), 2) add a custom Interceptor that does exponential backoff + jitter around network errors. For a quick workaround you can wrap calls with retry logic in the SDK.

maria: Tried 4.11.0 locally — behavior improved but still saw two near-instant retries on fast reconnects. Implemented local backoff wrapper and that stopped bursts.

jordan: Can you paste the minimal wrapper? We'll add it as an opt-in fix for the next release.

maria: Sure, quick pseudo-code: ```
fun <T> withJitterBackoff(retries: Int = 5, base: Long = 100) : (suspend ()->T) -> T = { call ->
  var attempt = 0
  while(true) {
    try { return call() }
    catch(e: IOException) {
      if (++attempt > retries) throw e
      val jitter = (Math.random() * base).toLong()
      val backoff = base * (1 shl (attempt - 1)) + jitter
      Thread.sleep(backoff)
    }
  }
}
```

sasha: Nice. Could we make that a low-level option in the SDK so apps don't have to? Might be a toggle like enableNetworkJitterBackoff=true.

alex: Agreed. We should add it behind a flag and ensure tests cover emulator/network flaps. Also file an engineering ticket to track the OkHttp upgrade + SDK option.

maria: Opening GH issue now and I'll attach the repro sampleapp (small changes). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-android/issues/451 (draft).

devx-bot: New issue created: sdk-android#451 — "okhttp: immediate retries on reconnect, missing jitter/backoff" (assigned to @maria).

jordan: Action items: 1) Add E2E test that toggles emulator network to validate jitter/backoff (owner: jordan), 2) Add SDK flag + opt-in default true for new minor (owner: alex), 3) Upgrade okhttp in separate PR and smoke test across Android 8–13 (owner: sasha).

maria: I'll attach the logs and minimal sample to the issue. Thanks all, gonna proceed with the wrapper PR as a stopgap. :thumbsup:

alex: Thanks — please add a short note in the release notes about the behavior and workaround so customers on older apps aren't surprised.

sasha: Also add a small snippet to the onboarding docs under "Network resilience on Android" so mobile integrators know about emulator flakiness and the flag.

maria: Will do. Closing thread once PR + issue have links in the ticket.
